fullPassage:
Stress not only affects physical disease but also the very structure of our brains, making us even more likely to experience a drained brain.

(C) A number of studies have been done to reveal what happens in healthy people's brains when they go through something stressful. One study demonstrated a link between a smaller hippocampus and people who had experienced long-lasting stress.

(A) Why does this matter? This part of the brain helps you remain resilient in the face of stress and is involved in mood regulation. It also helps you to monitor the safety of your environment and store dangerous images in your long-term memory so you can avoid them in the future.

(B) It does all these things as part of its duties of regulating your sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems. But chronic stress can confuse the hippocampus and lead to turning signals for cortisol 'on' instead of 'off,' which can trap you in a constant state of fight, flight, or freeze.

questions.passage: Stress not only affects physical disease but also the very structure of our brains, making us even more likely to experience a drained brain. (C) A number of studies have been done to reveal what happens in healthy people's brains when they go through something stressful. This part of the brain helps you remain (A)[resilient / vulnerable] in the face of stress and is involved in mood regulation. It also helps you to (B)[monitor / ignore] the safety of your environment and store dangerous images in your long-term memory so you can (C)[avoid / seek] them in the future. (B) It does all these things as part of its duties of regulating your sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems. But chronic stress can confuse the hippocampus and lead to turning signals for cortisol 'on' instead of 'off,' which can trap you in a constant state of fight, flight, or freeze.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 뇌의 이 부분은 스트레스에 (A)회복탄력적(resilient)이도록 돕고, 환경의 안전성을 (B)감시(monitor)하며, 위험 이미지를 저장해 미래에 (C)피할(avoid) 수 있게 한다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① vulnerable(취약한): resilient(회복탄력적)의 반의어
❌ ② ignore(무시하다): monitor(감시하다)의 반의어
❌ ③ seek(찾다): avoid(피하다)의 반의어
✅ ④ resilient — monitor — avoid: 원문과 일치 ←정답
det.tip: resilient(회복탄력적) ↔ vulnerable(취약한), monitor(감시) ↔ ignore(무시), avoid(피하다) ↔ seek(찾다)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 한 연구는 작은 해마와 장기 스트레스 경험자 사이의 연관성을 (A)입증했다(demonstrated). 해마는 교감/부교감 신경계를 (B)조절하는(regulating) 임무를 수행하지만, 만성 스트레스는 해마를 (C)혼란시킬(confuse) 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① demonstrated — regulating — confuse: 원문과 일치 ←정답
❌ ② concealed(숨긴): demonstrated(입증한)의 반의어
❌ ③ disrupting(방해하는): regulating(조절하는)의 반의어
❌ ④ clarify(명확히 하다): confuse(혼란시키다)의 반의어
det.tip: demonstrate(입증) ↔ conceal(숨기다), regulate(조절) ↔ disrupt(방해), confuse(혼란) ↔ clarify(명확히)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 건강한 사람의 뇌에서 일어나는 일을 (A)밝히기(reveal) 위한 연구들이 수행되었다. (B)오래 지속되는(long-lasting) 스트레스를 경험한 사람들의 해마가 더 작았다. 만성 스트레스는 (C)끊임없는(constant) 투쟁-도주-경직 상태에 갇히게 할 수 있다.
det.analysis:

❌ ② obscure(가리다): reveal(밝히다)의 반의어
✅ ③ reveal — long-lasting — constant: 원문과 일치 ←정답
❌ ④ temporary(일시적): constant(끊임없는)의 반의어
det.tip: reveal(밝히다) ↔ obscure(가리다), long-lasting(오래 지속) ↔ momentary(순간적), constant(끊임없는) ↔ temporary(일시적)

questions.passage: Stress not only ①<u>affects</u> physical disease but also the very structure of our brains, making us even more likely to experience a drained brain. A number of studies have been done to reveal what happens in healthy people's brains when they go through something ②<u>stressful</u>. One study demonstrated a link between a smaller hippocampus and people who had experienced long-lasting stress. Why does this matter? This part of the brain helps you remain ③<u>susceptible</u> in the face of stress and is involved in mood regulation. It also helps you to monitor the safety of your environment and ④<u>store</u> dangerous images in your long-term memory so you can avoid them in the future. It does all these things as part of its duties of regulating your sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems. But chronic stress can confuse the hippocampus and lead to turning signals for cortisol 'on' instead of 'off,' which can trap you in a constant state of fight, flight, or freeze.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ susceptible(영향받기 쉬운) → resilient(회복탄력적인): 해마는 스트레스에 '회복탄력적이도록' 돕는다는 맥락.
det.analysis:
✅ ① affects(영향을 미치다): 원문 일치
✅ ② stressful(스트레스를 주는): 원문 일치
❌ ③ susceptible(영향받기 쉬운): 원문은 resilient(회복탄력적인) — 반의어 ←정답
✅ ④ store(저장하다): 원문 일치
det.tip: resilient(회복탄력적) ↔ susceptible(영향받기 쉬운). remain resilient = 회복탄력성을 유지하다

det.korean: ② temporary(일시적인) → chronic(만성적인): '만성적인' 스트레스가 해마를 혼란시킨다는 맥락.

✅ ③ regulation(조절): 원문 일치

det.tip: chronic(만성적인) ↔ temporary(일시적인). chronic stress = 만성 스트레스

❌ ② (A) '점검하다'는 경기 중 관찰 맥락에 부적합
❌ ③ (B) '감시하다'는 환경 안전성을 능동적으로 확인한다는 맥락에 부적합
❌ ④ (A)도 '점검하다'는 부적합
det.tip: monitor: ① (사람/행동을) 감시하다, 지켜보다 ② (상태/상황을) 점검하다, 확인하다

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"a chemical substance produced in the body that controls and regulates the activity of certain cells or organs"

det.korean: 체내에서 생산되어 특정 세포나 기관의 활동을 조절하는 화학물질 = cortisol(코르티솔). 본문에서 스트레스 호르몬으로 언급.
det.analysis:
❌ ① enzyme(효소): 촉매 역할의 단백질
❌ ② neuron(신경세포): 신호 전달 세포
✅ ③ cortisol(코르티솔): 스트레스 호르몬, 영영풀이와 일치 ←정답
❌ ④ vitamin(비타민): 영양소
det.tip: cortisol = 코르티솔, 스트레스 호르몬. hormone(호르몬)의 한 종류

questions.passage: A number of studies have been done to reveal what happens in __________ (health) people's brains when they go through something stressful.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 명사 health(건강)를 형용사형 healthy(건강한)로 변환. 명사 people을 수식하므로 형용사가 필요.
det.analysis: ✅ healthy: health(명사) → healthy(형용사). healthy people = 건강한 사람들
det.tip: health(건강, 명사) → healthy(건강한, 형용사) → healthily(건강하게, 부사)

questions.passage: A number of studies have been done to reveal what happens in healthy people's brains when they go through something __________. (stress)
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 명사 stress(스트레스)를 형용사형 stressful(스트레스를 주는)로 변환. something 뒤 형용사 보어가 필요.
det.analysis: ✅ stressful: stress(명사) → stressful(형용사). something stressful = 스트레스를 주는 무언가
det.tip: stress(명사) → stressful(형용사, ~ful = ~으로 가득한). something + 형용사(후치수식)

questions.passage: Stress not only affects physical disease but also the very structure of our brains, making us even more likely to experience a drained brain. A number of studies have been done to reveal what happens in healthy people's brains when they go through something stressful. One study demonstrated a link between a smaller hippocampus and people who had experienced long-lasting stress. Why does this matter? This part of the brain helps you remain resilient in the face of stress and is involved in mood regulation. It also helps you to monitor the safety of your environment and store dangerous images in your __________ so you can avoid them in the future. It does all these things as part of its duties of regulating your sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems. But chronic stress can confuse the hippocampus and lead to turning signals for cortisol 'on' instead of 'off,' which can trap you in a constant state of fight, flight, or freeze.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 해마는 위험한 이미지를 장기 기억(long-term memory)에 저장하여 미래에 피할 수 있게 돕는다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① long-term memory(장기 기억): 원문과 일치, 위험 이미지를 저장하는 곳 ←정답
❌ ② mood regulation(기분 조절): 본문에 있지만 이미지를 저장하는 곳이 아님
❌ ③ physical disease(신체 질병): 본문에 있지만 문맥 부적합
❌ ④ long-lasting stress(오래 지속되는 스트레스): 본문에 있지만 저장 장소가 아님
det.tip: long-term memory = 장기 기억. store images in your long-term memory = 장기 기억에 이미지를 저장하다

questions.passage: Stress not only affects physical disease but also the very structure of our brains, making us even more likely to experience a drained brain. A number of studies have been done to reveal what happens in healthy people's brains when they go through something stressful. One study demonstrated a link between a smaller hippocampus and people who had experienced long-lasting stress. Why does this matter? This part of the brain helps you remain resilient in the face of stress and is involved in __________. It also helps you to monitor the safety of your environment and store dangerous images in your long-term memory so you can avoid them in the future. It does all these things as part of its duties of regulating your sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems. But chronic stress can confuse the hippocampus and lead to turning signals for cortisol 'on' instead of 'off,' which can trap you in a constant state of fight, flight, or freeze.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 뇌의 이 부분은 스트레스에 회복탄력적이도록 돕고 기분 조절(mood regulation)에 관여한다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① physical disease(신체 질병): 본문에 있지만 해마의 기능이 아님
❌ ② long-lasting stress(오래 지속되는 스트레스): 본문에 있지만 해마의 기능이 아님
❌ ③ long-term memory(장기 기억): 본문에 있지만 '관여(involved in)'의 대상은 기분 조절
✅ ④ mood regulation(기분 조절): 원문과 일치 ←정답
det.tip: mood regulation = 기분 조절. is involved in mood regulation = 기분 조절에 관여하다
